name: EMA / IIR Coefficient Tool
blurb: smoothing coefficient from a cutoff frequency, with the response drawn
intro: The first-order low-pass y += α (x − y), sampled at fs. From a cutoff it gives α (either the exact −3 dB point or the matched RC time constant), from α or a right shift it gives the cutoff; the magnitude and step responses are drawn from the filter's own transfer function α / (1 − (1 − α) z⁻¹).

examples.title: 10 Hz smoothing on a 1 kHz sensor loop
What does y += (x - y) >> 4 do at 200 Hz?

usage: Choose mode cutoff (give fs and fc in Hz and method exact or rc), alpha (give α between 0 and 1) or shift (give k, α = 1/2^k). It returns α, the −3 dB frequency, the time constant in samples and seconds, samples to settle to 63/95/99 %, the white-noise variance reduction, the nearest shift and Q15 constants, C code, and the magnitude (dB) and step-response curves as chart data. Use it to pick a firmware smoothing filter from a wanted bandwidth or to see what an existing α does.
sources: Exact −3 dB point of y[n] = α x[n] + (1 − α) y[n−1]: α = cos ω − 1 + √(cos²ω − 4 cos ω + 3), ω = 2π fc / fs, from |H(e^jω)|² = 1/2 (standard derivation, e.g. dsp.stackexchange 'exponential weighted moving average time constant')
Matched time constant α = 1 − e^(−2π fc / fs): impulse invariance of an RC low-pass, Oppenheim & Schafer, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, ch. 7
Noise variance ratio α / (2 − α): sum of the squared impulse response α (1 − α)^n
